text:
priya: quick q — can we add a route-level 'quick filters' feature in Console analytics so teams can pin a small set of filters that persist per-route? saved queries are global and really noisy rn

alex: we talked about something similar last sprint. main complexity is scope/ownership. global saved queries are simple, per-route defaults need owner, visibility, and a migration path for existing links

taylor: from a UX pov: surface three scopes: personal / team / org. small toggle next to the query bar. mock idea: 
```
[ scope: (You) v (Team) v (Org) ]  [ Save as default ]
```
keep it inline so it doesn't add chrome

jamie: technical note — beware deep links. we currently accept query params in url. precedence propose: url params > user pinned default > team pinned default > org default > route saved query library. simple rule avoids surprises

sam: +1 on precedence. data note: saved queries adoption is low but bookmarks per-route are ~12% of active routes. small win if we make pinning obvious

mel: UX copy idea: a tiny chip, "Pin filters for this route" with confirmation modal explaining scope and who can unpin. :pin:

alex: DB/infra sketch: need route_default_filters table with columns: route_id, owner_id, scope(enum personal/team/org), filter_expr, created_at. migration: move top N popular saved queries into org scope? also consider cleanup for orphaned owners

jamie: sample precedence pseudocode:
```
function applyFilters(route, urlParams, user) {
  if (urlParams) return urlParams
  if (user.hasPinned(route)) return user.pinned[route]
  if (user.team.hasPinned(route)) return user.team.pinned[route]
  if (org.hasPinned(route)) return org.pinned[route]
  return route.defaultLibraryQuery
}
```

priya: permissions question — who can pin at team/org level? only org admins or can team leads do it? i lean admin for org, team-lead or route-owner for team scope

jamie: agree. implement RBAC: roles route_owner, team_admin, org_admin. enforce on server side for set/unset endpoints

sam: telemetry we need: events: route_filter_pin_set, route_filter_pin_applied, route_filter_unset, route_filter_fallback_used. include route_id, scope, user_id, and whether url param overrode. also track signal for default usage so we can measure adoption

mel: i'll sketch the modal and post a Figma link in #design after standup. will include copy for the confirm ("This will make these filters the default for X — users in scope will see them automatically")

alex: backend tasks: schema + migration + API endpoints: POST /routes/:id/pins, GET /routes/:id/pins, DELETE /routes/:id/pins. will add feature-flag gate: feature_flag=route_quick_filters. plan: canary 10% orgs -> 50% -> all. need to add audit log entries for changes

priya: rollout + QA: start with internal org + 2 pilot customers. QA checklist: deep link behavior, RBAC, telemetry, db migration idempotence, UI fallback for routes with no pins

jamie: warning: some routes are high-traffic and we evaluate filters server-side for pre-agg. might need caching and TTL for computed views. sam, can we add quota/compute estimate?

sam: yes — appying pinned defaults adds little cpu per request, but if we auto-recompute aggregated metrics per-route when pin changes we may spike. recommend asynchronous recompute with rate limit and queue. add per-tenant rollout to control load

priya: acceptance criteria (draft):
- UI toggle to pin/unpin filters with scope selector
- Server endpoints with RBAC and audit logs
- Precedence rules implemented (url > personal > team > org > library)
- Telemetry events emitted
- Feature flag + canary rollout plan + migration script

alex: timeline estimate: backend + migration 2 wks, frontend + UX polish 1.5 wks, telemetry + rollout 3 days. target merge end of sprint + 2 weeks for full rollout if no issues

mel: i'll prototype modal and send screenshots. tagging @eng-platform for API contract review

priya: awesome — i'll add to the roadmap and create a GH issue with those ACs and link this thread. thanks all :sparkles:

alex: i'll start a PR for schema change and post branch link here when ready

jamie: +1, will stub the client-side precedence logic and tests.

sam: i'll add telemetry spec + sample queries to the GH issue

mel: :thumbsup:

bot-deploy: feature_flag route_quick_filters enabled for org-id:internal-canary
